On Sun, Aug 28, 2016 at 9:48 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
[back on stan-dev]

I'm working on it, so please don't jump in now, Daniel.

Got it.

I'm still playing catchup. Friday was good, then I fell asleep all yesterday.

What I really need to know is how the probability test framework
works for invalid values.  If it's easier for you to go fishing
and create a wiki, let me know when it's up.

Here's a quick summary. I'll go put up a wiki page for full details. It's a mess because it's a lot of crazy templating and code generation, but here we go.


1. The developer writes a test header. It'll be something like: test/prob/wiener/wiener_test.hpp. It will be a *.hpp.
  A. The first line has a comment line that looks like: "// Arguments: Doubles, Doubles, Doubles, Doubles, Doubles"
       This is used by the test generator to tell how to generate the C++ test files. (this is a bit of a mess.) Valid things to use there are "Double", "Doubles", "Int", "Ints"
  B. Create a test class that extends AgradDistributionTest.
  C. valid_values() puts those values (should be called "arguments") into the function and verifies that it works. Each valid thing is a std::vector<double> of the length of argument.
  D. invalid_values() takes one set of the valid ones and then inserts the invalid argument into the std::vector in the location specified and checks for error.
  E. log_prob() is the way the test takes the std::vector<double> and calls the correct function to test. There are two of them, one for no propto argument, the other with one.
  F. log_prob_function() is the way we compare with another implementation, like autodiff. We should probably get rid of this now.

2. There's a cpp executable that generates all the template instantiations split into multiple files. This is test/prob/generate_tests.cpp. From the math library, if you type `make test/prob/generate_tests`, it'll build just that executable.

3. The test header is passed to the built test/prob/generate_tests with a number of template instantiations to keep within each test file. It'll look something like:

test/prob/generate_tests test/prob/wiener/wiener_test.hpp 100

This is going to generate a ton of tests like:

test/prob/wiener/wiener_00126_generated_ffv_test.cpp

4. ./runTests.py will just run all the tests in that folder or that single test, just like it does for all the rest of the unit tests.


And yes, it's a mess. I think it can be done a lot better now that I've done it once. One of the reasons it can't be done at runtime is cause it needs the template instantiations. And we have this terrible interaction with google test.

The reason we split test instantiations is due to compilers just taking way too much ram and failing tests.

Otherwise, what I really want to know is how the invalid_values()
tests work.  Is each value tested independently?  And if so,
how are the other arguments filled in?  Because if they're filled
in with the valid values, I can use that to test.

But I'll just hardcode a unit test for the distribution now because
I really want to clear out all these lingering pull requests that
nobody has time to finish.

I also think "values" is the wrong argument here---they are argument
tests, not result tests, and to me, "value" implies result (in y = f(x),
y is the result and x is the argument---"value" is too vague).  Anyway,
this is totally minor compared to understanding how the tests
actually work.

- Bob
